324618.title: Equality of the Terwilliger and orbit centralizer algebras for the conjugacy scheme of the symmetric group
324618.literal_statement:
Let $O_1,\dots,O_M$ be the orbits of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)^2$ under $\operatorname{Iso}_1(n)$, and let $B_i$ be the corresponding zero-one matrices. Let $\mathfrak{T}$ denote the Terwilliger algebra of the conjugacy scheme of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$, and let $\mathfrak{B}=\langle B_i:i=1,\dots,M\rangle$. **Equality conjecture.** The matrices $B_i$, $i=1,\dots,M$, form a basis of $\mathfrak{T}$; equivalently, as $\mathbb{C}$-algebras,

$$
\mathfrak{T}=\mathfrak{B}.
$$

The preceding discussion establishes the inclusion $\mathfrak{T}\subseteq\mathfrak{B}$, while the reverse inclusion is described as reasonable but substantially more difficult to prove. Thus the equality remains open in the source.
324618.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Orbit indicators require full reverse inclusion for every n. Generation by conjugacy adjacency and dual idempotents does not by itself span every simultaneous-isometry orbit. No explicit missing-orbit functional or generation induction proved; primary Iso_1 definition unread.

324758.title: Sarwate's conjecture on Fourier coefficients of power permutations
324758.literal_statement:
Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic $2$ with $q=|L|$, and let $f(x)=x^s$ be a power permutation of $L$. Define its Fourier coefficients by

$$
\widehat f(a)=\sum_{x\in L}\mu(ax+f(x)).
$$

**Sarwate's conjecture.** If $[L:{\mathbb F}_2]$ is even, then

$$
\sup_{a\in L}\widehat f(a)\geq 2\sqrt q.
$$

The source identifies this as Sarwate's main global conjecture and explicitly says that it is still open; it follows discussion of results proving an earlier characteristic-two conjecture.
324758.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Parseval yields a sqrt(q)-scale lower bound, not positive coefficient >=2sqrt(q) for every even extension degree and every invertible exponent. 334452.title: Galvin's biregular homomorphism conjecture
334452.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph, let $d_u$ denote the degree of $u\in V(G)$, and let $H$ be a loop-graph. Write $\hom(G,H)$ for the number of graph homomorphisms from $G$ to $H$. **Galvin's biregular homomorphism conjecture.**

$$
\hom(G,H)\le \prod_{uv\in E(G)}\hom(K_{d_u,d_v},H)^{1/(d_ud_v)}.
$$

This would extend the regular and biregular homomorphism inequalities, as well as the bipartite case of Kahn's irregular independent-set conjecture. Its status is open.

Local regular/biregular bounds cannot simply be multiplied for overlapping stars. The same-source historical triangle-free/regular/coloring questions are different targets; isolated vertices also need source conventions. No full proof or witness.

354571.title: The 2-balanced double tree decomposition conjecture
354571.literal_statement:
A **double tree** is a graph formed by taking two trees on the same vertex set, with the two edge sets regarded as distinct even when they join the same pair of vertices. A **double tree decomposition** partitions the edges of a double tree into two trees. Such a decomposition is **$k$-balanced** if, at every vertex, the absolute difference between its degrees in the two trees is at most $k$.

**2-balanced double tree decomposition conjecture.** Any double tree has a $2$-balanced double tree decomposition.

The paper proves that every double tree has a decomposition that is $4$-balanced, improving the previously known bound of five. Examples are known that admit a $2$-balanced decomposition but no $1$-balanced one, so the conjectured bound would be best possible; the conjecture remains open.

354623.title: Eliahou–Villarreal conjecture on projective dimension of edge ideals
354623.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertices $V(G)=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$, let $R=\mathbb{K}[x\mid x\in V(G)]$, and let $I(G)=(x_ix_j\mid \{x_i,x_j\}\in E(G))$ be its edge ideal. The quotient $R/I(G)=\mathbb{K}[\Delta_G]$ has a 2-linear resolution when its minimal graded free resolution has the form

$$
0 \longrightarrow R(-2-p)^{\beta_p} \longrightarrow \cdots\longrightarrow R(-3)^{\beta_1} \longrightarrow R(-2)^{\beta_0} \longrightarrow R \longrightarrow \mathbb{K}[\Delta_G] \longrightarrow 0.
$$

**Eliahou–Villarreal conjecture.** If the edge ideal of a connected graph $G$ has a 2-linear resolution, then

$$
\operatorname{pdim}(R/I(G))=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}\{\deg_G(x_i)\}.
$$

By Fröberg's theorem, the 2-linear-resolution hypothesis is equivalent to $G$ being co-chordal in the convention used here. The paper states that this conjecture is false in general and constructs counterexamples; it also proves the equality for several subclasses, including sequentially Cohen–Macaulay co-chordal graphs and graphs with a full vertex.

354853.title: The almost-stable Kneser hypergraph colorability bound
354853.literal_statement:

$$
\chi\left(\operatorname{KG}^r\left(\mathcal G_{\widetilde{\{s\text{-stable}\}}}\right)\right)\geq\left\lceil\frac{\operatorname{cd}^r(\mathcal G)}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture is proposed in the paper as a partial answer to a problem concerning how large the gap between the colorability-defect bound and the chromatic number can be. The supplied text gives no resolution.

354960.title: Generic codimension additivity for subdivisions of graphical-model supports
354960.literal_statement:
Assume that $\dim(\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}})=d$. Let

$$
h=\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}(G)}h_{\mathcal{X}_C,y_C}.
$$

Let $\sigma$ be the subdivision of $\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$ induced by $h$, and let $\sigma_C$ be the subdivision of $\pi_C(\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}})$ induced by $h_{\mathcal{X}_C,y_C}$. For $z\in\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$, let $k_z$ and $l_z$ be the codimensions of the minimal faces of $\sigma$ and $\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$ containing $z$, respectively. For each $C\in\mathcal{C}(G)$, let $k_{z,C}$ and $l_{z,C}$ be the codimensions of the minimal faces of $\sigma_C$ and $\pi_C(\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}})$ containing $z_C$, respectively.

**Generic codimension additivity conjecture.** If $\mathcal{S}_{G,\mathcal{X}}$ and all tent functions $h_{\mathcal{X}_C,y_C}$ are sufficiently generic, then

$$
k_z-l_z=\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}(G)}k_{z,C}-\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}(G)}l_{z,C}.
$$

The preceding corollary proves only the corresponding inequality for the subdivision codimensions. The generic equality is presented as a conjectural strengthening and concerns the combinatorics of intersections of clique-wise regular subdivisions.
354960.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Sufficiently generic has no quantified exceptional set in the literal. Pullbacks of clique subdivision faces may share coordinate dependencies, so naive transversality is insufficient. Need actual support/tent definitions and relative-boundary codimension calculation at every z. Neither a genericity theorem nor counterexample proved.

381126.title: The global linkage characterization conjecture for rigid graphs
381126.literal_statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a rigid graph and let $u,v\in V$. A pair of vertices is **globally linked** if every generic realisation of $G$ determines the distance between its two vertices. **Global linkage characterization conjecture.** The pair $\\{u,v\\}$ is globally linked in $G$ if and only if either $uv\in E$ or $u$ and $v$ are joined by three internally disjoint paths in some ${\mathcal{RM}}$-connected component of $G$. This would characterize when two vertices in a rigid graph are globally linked; the corresponding result is known when the whole graph is ${\mathcal{RM}}$-connected, but the general rigid-graph case remains open.
381126.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Rigidity dimension and RM-connected components require source definitions. Need necessity and sufficiency for every rigid graph and every pair, beyond the known RM-connected case. Gluing components can preserve local distances without giving the asserted globally linked equivalence; no proved component reduction. Primary body unread.
